"Procedural audio" means sound effects that are generated by a computer program on the fly, rather than played back from a pre-recorded file — useful in games because the same footstep or explosion sound can vary slightly every time instead of feeling repetitive. "Spatial audio" means sound that is processed so it seems to come from a specific direction and distance around the listener, like a real 3D space, rather than flat stereo. This patent covers a method for automatically generating procedural sound effects that already carry the correct spatial positioning, so game engines can produce large amounts of directional sound without needing an artist to place each one by hand.
